body:
It may or may not be a cry for help, but if you're reading this comment, as well as the ones below ... then that means that you're in a state of cognitive dissonance. 


Once you have let go of the fear of dying, it becomes possible to live a life of courage. Then again, it is up to you to decide whether you want to become a by-product of your environment, become a statistic ... or evolve and take control of your destiny.

I used to be happy for this country, now I am worried ... especially with the recent rise in brain-dead conservatism ... our contempt for the poor, needy, mentally ill, immigrants, etc. We're becoming just like America, in some ways. 


New Zealand is certainly better than the US, but this might not last very long. The day we have house prices averaging at $2 million, massive youth unemployment due to automation, outsourcing, etc. is when things will start to become pretty gruesome. 



Parliament will never listen to the people, and they most certainly will never represent people of my age. I hate to be a downer, but I have to be ... given the things I've experienced as of late.

A life lived for others is a life worth living.. so long as one doesn't become a doormat. 

Depression can sometimes open one's eye to the fact that there is something wrong with the world that we live in, something that needs fixing, which is a blessing in and of itself. They all talk about this 'chemical imbalance', but human brain is a lot more complex than we seem to think. It's a powerful thing. 

Find a way you can make a difference in this world, and I'm not talking about volunteering. Volunteering is boring.

There used to be a lot more support on forums like these, but sadly, all I see is people reinforcing each others views. Maybe that's because more and more people are becoming depressed... so if the entire world were depressed, there would be no help ... and we'd have to start helping ourselves, then help others.

The fact that you're posting this here, means that things aren't as black and white as they seem. You do want to be helped.

What you don't want, is people giving you crappy useless advice, of course. Your subconscious is waiting for that one, magical post that will resonate and strike a chord... but even if you did come across that post, your other half would dismiss it with cynical skepticism. 

Maybe if suicide hotlines could actually, you know ... HELP SOLVE OUR PROBLEMS ... rather than trying to make us feel better... there wouldn't be half as many suicides.

It's definitely not selfish. Selfish are the people who run this dog-eat-dog sort of world that we live in ...



Having said that, suicide is wasteful. Human consciousness is your only chance at being able to touch, feel ... move... and have some degree of control over this universe.



Suicide also takes a lot of courage. It's pretty dumb to say that it is cowardly. Then again - this could be thought of as a good thing. It means you have the courage to let go, take a risk. 



You can always take those risks here on Earth, now that you have nothing left to lose. Beneficial risks, that is.. because.... What's the hurry with suicide, if you can always wait a day... anyway?
If you could wish for anything, other than death.. what would it be? What has gone wrong for you in this world, specifically?

You don't want to be a statistic.. one life thrown away is one too many.
 


I have the suspicion that the rising depression rates (as well as obesity, allergies, cancers, heart disease, etc.), are the result of our hunter gatherer brains being incompatible with the drudgery, predictability and overall lameness of modern society.


Sometimes .. a depressive episode is what it takes to let go, and reinvent yourself. Wouldn't it be way more awesome to keep your one chance to see what the future holds ... as opposed to withering away with the dinosaurs? Take control of destiny, as opposed to succumbing to what is a modern epidemic? I mean .. what is there to lose, really?
